label: SCRAM-SHA
type: the salted challenge-response authentication mechanism family Couchbase Server offers as the alternative to PLAIN, so that a password is never sent in the clear. Requires PBKDF2 password hashing to be available, and is what half-secure XDCR uses to protect the target cluster's password when the target runs Enterprise Server 5.5 or later.
evidence: This is either PLAIN or one of the revisions of SCRAM-SHA challenge-response mechanisms for authentication.
_PBKDF2_ is another powerful password hashing function; and is required to allow SCRAM-SHA capability.
By hashing with SCRAM-SHA, when the destination cluster is running Couchbase Enterprise Server 5.5 or later.
note: Reaches the bar only because an XDCR procedure page names it: the security reference introduces it, and the operational consequence - that a half-secure replication's password protection depends on SCRAM-SHA and therefore on the TARGET cluster's version - appears in manage-xdcr/. A version dependency that lives on the far side of a replication is not something the mechanism's own reference page would state.
